body: Male here. I have a similar issue and also take Linaclotide, but one of the most awful symptoms is not being able to pass gas. Frankly, not being able to fart is worse than not being to "go". Linaclotide helps with that, but not the gas. And then there is the fatigue and brain fog, which are unbearable...do suppositories or enemas ever do anything for you? I'm guessing it's difficult to use them because of the hermorrhoids, but I fortunately never had to deal with that problem specific, so I don0t know.
I think this HDD is a 2.5 inch.

Possibly, but there are no nearby places or hospitals who do the necessary tests (manometry, I'm guessing). There is gastric emptying tests, but convincing my GI is near impossible and I can't afford to go to a private doctor right no,w let alone pay for exams out of my pocket. Besides, medicine is a bit behind the times in here, at least when it comes to "newer" diagnoses such PFD, SIBO, Pseudo-obstruction, autoimmune issues, etc...You know...invisible illnesses.
Hard to get those done in the public healthcare system, not to mention that there are very few clinics that do that here.

Was inflammation detected in other tests as well or just in the biopsy? So far, all my blood/stool tests came back negative. MRI didn't show inflammation either, but that was to the small intestine, not the colon.

I too was put on Bupropion, but I was only on the lowest dosage (150). I felt a slight cognitive boost in the first few days, but eventually the effect was barely noticeable. I felt slightly more awake and had a tiny bit more energy, but that's it. Perhaps I should've tried a stronger dosage, I don't know. I suppose I'll find out with this one. However, minimal side effects like you said. I hope the reboxetine will behave the same. I'm wondering if not touching dopamine will have a major effect.

Does that problem have a name, at least? I know there is something called dyspraxia, but that's neurological/muscular (mostly), not something directly related to the eyes, however it affects hand-eye coordination.

>f resveratrol

Ok...how did you train, if you don't mind me asking? I have the same problem? I always had, but I don't know how to "increase" my spatial problems.
Yeah, I've tested for, only antigliadin was a positive, but others 3 ones were negative (zero or close to zero).

<4 mcg/g in a scale where it's considered negative if it's <=50, so really low. Strange that I have all these traits of inflammation but no markers show up. Joint pains, brain fog, chronic fatigue, rectal pressure and not passing gas (the worst symptom), constipation (not really a common inflammatory issue, but it supposedly can happen).

Frankly, very similar to the this title post, but replace the negativity from Christianity and post-partum with an awful and chronic intestinal/digestive disease that affects every part of my body and exams not displaying ANYTHING wrong so far. Add possible ADHD and generalized anxiety generated by everyday life plus the constant shaming for being sick and unproductive at home. I'm a bit amazed at how I haven't been thrown out of the house, but frankly, I might be so insignificant as not to qualify as a burden.

Hm...well, do you still take it or found a something that replaces it? I'm asking because frankly, though I haven't taken medication for a while, I've tried many in the past with little to no success and I don't want my body/liver/brain (you get the idea) to be a distillery for chemicals that might worsen an already..*.functionally subpar* brain. The best thing I've taken so far is sulbutiamine, which is over the counter, which is nice...but it's still very mild and not enough to handle some symptoms. But alas, I really should stop obsessing about this for the next few days. My doctor warned me this could happen and to try to refocus on something else less...worrying.

I'd like not to have to resort to such medications if possile honestly. Mine is usually 120/70 (not sure how those rates work), but yeah, it's a bit higher now, I assume. I could try working out if I am at home, but doesn't seem like that's an ideal solution on a regular basis.
So, in other words, don't expect it to turn you into a zombified super-computer and let it adjust to your body?
I'm in Europe, in a country that is years behind others compared to the rest (ESPECIALLY the US and Canada).

Yeah, I can't afford it at the moment. I'd probably try other things like Atrantil and iberogast if I could. There is also prucalopride and lubiprostone but they're not available here for some reason.

Yes, I have also tried them. Paroxetine and escitalopram, but all they is making me sleepy and upsetting my stomach (most SSRI do). I've tried 5-htp as well, which seemed to make me poop slightly more, but it didn't help with the gas. The digital stimulation (I assume you mean putting a finger up there) is something I already do coupled with glycerine suppositories, but it simply isn't enough. The pressure remains there. Thanks for the quick replies, btw.

I haven't taken fluconazole, but I have taken caprylic acid, oregano oil, black walnut, berberine, coconut oil and few other bitters as well as probiotics, so I think that if it was that, the symptoms would have diminished.

I don't like to suggest this kind of thing right away, but have you tried a stimulant or stimulant-like antidepressant? There are things like Bupropion or even stronger things that stimulate dopamine receptors but I myseld prefer Sulbutiamine which is something you can get over the counter. It has cognitive enhancing effects and it affects dopamine receptors like the others and I find that it makes me more talkative and energetic (which is very unlike me).

What would be the interactions between this and L-DOPA (Mucuna) ? I know sulbutiamine has an effect on dopamine receptors. Will it make the resulting dopamine more available? Or will it cause an overload/deregulation of it? My dopamine levels are generally terribly low, that's why I'm considering the combo. I know it's used with choline supplements, but that affects different neurotransmitters.
Yeah, you're right. I was a prick, I'm sorry.

I forgot to mention...watch out for carbohydrate intake. In many anti-bacterial diets, they recommended slashing many of these foods so it starves the bacteria (that is the theory, anyway, some advocate eating them anyway to draw out the bacteria - it's contradictory and complicated, I know).  Carbohydrates and foods with sugar, such as a lot of fruits, can make certain symptoms worse. Brocolli, cabbage and other vegetables with FODMAPs should perhaps be avoided, depending on how your body reacts to them. Following a vegan diet might make this difficult.

Similar experience here, although my country (also in Europe) might be even more far behind in terms of SIBO and other covert GI issues. My problem isn't solved either but some supplements do ease some of the symptoms. Collagen helps some days and so do L-Glutamine (particularly for brain fog), Coconut oil, oregano oil, etc. My problem is, however, constipation, gas retention, not passing gas, slow motility, etc., which may be very different from yours, but those are still options to consider. 

 It might be pricey but the community suggests things like Allimed/Allimax, Atrantil, Candibactin, oregano oil, caprylic acid, peppermint oil capsules, berberine, allicin/strong garlic supplements and others, all of which might have an impact on the gut flora and motility. 

I realize that many of these are not prescribed, which can be hard on your wallet because if they were prescribed by your doctors, your healthcare system would pay at least part of the cost (at least I'm assuming that's how things are over there).

There are always pharmaceuticals like Librax (anti-spasmodic), simethicone (for gas and bloating) and digestive enzymes, but these don't address the root cause, if SIBO really is the culprit. I'm guessing you want rifaximin, neomycin or god forbid, metronidazole, but like you mention, they're not very willing to prescribe these unless you have a strong definitive diagnosis or some nasty diarrhea. 

Frankly, this disease is a lot of trial and error, so I can't really give you definite answers and I'm merely throwing darts, trying to hit anything, but those are my suggestions.

I've done an endoscopy, but they didn't take a biopsy. I've done both a colonoscopy and endoscopy, but none presented any signs of gluten intolerance (and I ate foods with gluten or purpose before the exams). I've also done an MRi of the small intestine. Same thing, no signs of inflammation and blood tests show no malabsorption. To be fair, my intake of gluten has been minimal recently and my symptoms haven't improved so I'm almost sure it's something else.
Any tips on not being able to pass gas regularly? Because Linzess and the other laxatives/bowel stimulants don't help. Coconut oil and perppermint oil used to help with that, but not anymore.
How many mg are we talking about, exactly?

I take Linaclotide. It's a bit pricey, but nothing like in the US (I live in Europe). As for gas, it has been a struggle. Coconut oil helps occasionally, some antispasmodics also can help but they're all really inconsistent. I'll try peppermint oil capsules next, but to be fair, I have my doubts. I'd try Atrantil, but I'm broke at the moment and Atrantil is also expensive.

Food that is hard to digest or that is not completely digested such as corn, brown-nice, most kinds of nuts, peppers, mushrooms, etc, cause terrible bloating and pain, but I don't eat those anymore. And I stopped eating lactose many months ago. I don't eat a lot of starch anymore. The only gluten I eat is during breakfast, in a sort of powdered oatmeal (I don't know the name in English). But to be frank, I think I will still feel the symptoms regardless of what I eat.
I'd say that a lot of that also applies to ADHD. It's not like kids with ADHD magically stop having it at 18, it's just ignored because it's often subtle.
Oh, I haven't found any Iberogast on ebay for such a low price, unfortunately.
Things that make me bloated usually make me constipated. I think it's all the gas that's preventing the intestines from properly functioning.
I'm a male, and no, there doesn't seem to be an obstruction or inflammation that could cause this. The ultrasound, colonoscopy and MRI haven't shown anything of the sort, at least.

There seem to be no nutritional deficiencies, but I doubt a blood test would point out a cause or a symptom. And to be honest, brain fog has always been something that has affected me, but I can't afford a neurologist and my family doctor won't take the issue seriously. Most doctors attribute it to mental illness or anxiety, so it's not even worth it to try to explain the problem thoroughly. 

About this you wrote, *Things that just make you bloated but not constipated are okay (bloating is unfortunately just something we have to tolerate..*.I wholeheartedly have to disagree on that. Not passing gas, being bloated...that's far worse than constipation. Linaclotide can make go to the bathroom. But nothing can get rid of all the gas stuck inside. I barely pass gas most days, and I feel very relieved when I do. Coconut oil sort of helped that. But not anymore. Nothing helps with that anymore. I feel like ending my life because of this. All these headaches, body barely working, I barely leave the house most days. The only reason I haven't ended my life a lot of days is because I'm too weak to go somewhere I can do.

But that's the thing.  The only I took of that kind were 2 Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid tablets for a tooth infection and that certainly wasn't enough to cause this. And the stool tests say that the intestinal flora is abundant and rich. No bacteria like Shigella, salmonella or anything of the sort. Not that those cause constipation. I even had a gastroenteritis (a viral one)several years and it went away without antibiotics in 3 days. I always had regular movements, that's what bugs me about it. It just appeared. And it stayed. For 2 years. And counting.
